summary:
The needle: `/workspace/migrations/002_rename_status.sql` renamed the `status` column to `order_status`, but `app/main.go` still referenced the old `status` name in both the `INSERT` (createOrder) and `SELECT` (getOrder) queries — a classic schema-drift bug that would make every order create/fetch fail with `column "status" does not exist`.

**Fix applied** (`app/main.go`): updated both queries to use `order_status`, matching the current schema, and rebuilt `/workspace/orders-api`.

**Verification:** `test.sh` requires `su postgres`, which needs root — the current shell only has the unprivileged `bench` account (no sudo, no setuid path, no root capabilities available), so `test.sh` itself can't run in this session regardless of the code fix. To verify the actual fix, I spun up a disposable Postgres instance as `bench`, applied the same three migrations, pointed a temporary build of the app at it, and hit the real HTTP endpoints:
- `POST /orders` → 200, returned `order_status: "pending"`
- `GET /orders/1` → 200, returned the same order with `order_status` intact

Both match what `test.sh` asserts. I cleaned up the temporary instance afterward; the real `/workspace/orders-api` binary is rebuilt with the fix and ready for `test.sh` to run in an environment with root/postgres access.
